en: The Basket of Conduct (Cariyāpiṭaka), Chapter on Yudhañjaya:
The Perfection of Renunciation (Nekkhammapāramī) 1
The Story of Yudhañjaya:
“When I was Prince Yudhañjaya of immeasurable fame, ...”
Having seen a drop of dew fallen in the heat of the sun, I was struck with awe;
making that very thing my primary object of focus, I reflected.
I cultivated a sense of spiritual urgency;
having paid homage to my mother and father,
I requested permission for the going forth.
With palms joined together,
the people of the towns and the provinces entreat me:
“Son, practice [the holy life] this very day.”
Prosperous, flourishing, and very great—
along with its king, its harem,
its townspeople, and its provinces.
While they lamented piteously,
I abandoned them all without looking back,
even the entire earth and its sovereignty.
Relinquishing my kinsmen, retinue, and fame, I did not worry,
solely for the sake of awakening.
My mother and father are not to be given away by me,
nor is my great fame to be given away;
omniscience alone is dear to me.
"Therefore, he renounced his kingdom.
This is the first account, the Life of Yudhañjaya.
